messages.subject: Re: problem in recovery
messages.body_plain:
Dear Tarek,

I'm not sure this has to do with irace. It seems an error message given by another package (doSnow?): https://github.com/tobigithub/R-parallel/wiki/R-parallel-Errors#error-error-in-summaryconnectionconnection--invalid-connection

I see that you got the error also at the top of your screenshot before running.

1. Try launching irace from a fresh R console without running anything else before it.

2. Do not launch any parallel stuff or load any parallel libraries before launching irace. If you want irace to run in parallel, you have to use the options provided by irace, otherwise, it will not work.

Let us know if any of the above fixes the issue so that we can add it to the FAQ.

Best wishes,

Manuel.

messages.subject: Re: Problem in t-test
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tarek,

The error means that the values compared are almost constant so the t-test in R complains. However, irace is able to handle that case and the error is ignored:

    # t.test may fail if the data in each group is almost constant. Hence, we
    # surround the call in a try() and we initialize p with 1 if the means are
    # equal or zero if they are different
    if (min(var(results_best), var(results_j)) < 10 * .Machine$double.eps) next

But I did a few experiments  and I cannot even get the error to show up. Would it be possible to send us the output of irace when you run with --debug-level 3? This will show us what numbers your program is returning to irace.

The choice between t-test and F-test is not about homogeneous or heterogeneous scenario, it is about how you will compare two different configurations: are you comparing the mean performance or are you comparing based on "wins" or "ranks"? Or in other words, do you care about outliers or not?

Also, what version of irace and what version of R is this?

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.subject: Re: problem in recovery
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tarek,

Could you run without parallel? That is, set parallel=0. It seems that the debug output is not shown in Windows when running in parallel (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/56501937/how-to-print-from-clusterapply). Without the debug output, I don't know if irace is waiting for your algorithm to finish running or there is a bug in irace. I don't have Windows and this works fine in Linux.

You don't need to run also the recovery.

Cheers,

Manuel.
